question_text: A 42-year-old man presents to his primary care provider complaining of foamy urine for the last 2 weeks. He has also begun to notice swelling in his hands and feet, and he says that his shoes have not been fitting normally. On exam, the patient has a temperature of 98.8°F (37.1°C), blood pressure is 132/84 mmHg, pulse is 64/min, and respirations are 12/min. The patient has 2+ pitting edema bilaterally up to his shins. A 24-hour urine study is found to contain 9.0 g of protein. The patient is referred to a specialist and undergoes a renal biopsy. On light microscopy, the glomeruli demonstrate basement membrane thickening. On electron microscopy, subepithelial deposits are seen. Which of the following is a characteristic of this patient’s disease?

                    ### Question
                    A 42-year-old man presents to his primary care provider complaining of foamy urine for the last 2 weeks. He has also begun to notice swelling in his hands and feet, and he says that his shoes have not been fitting normally. On exam, the patient has a temperature of 98.8°F (37.1°C), blood pressure is 132/84 mmHg, pulse is 64/min, and respirations are 12/min. The patient has 2+ pitting edema bilaterally up to his shins. A 24-hour urine study is found to contain 9.0 g of protein. The patient is referred to a specialist and undergoes a renal biopsy. On light microscopy, the glomeruli demonstrate basement membrane thickening. On electron microscopy, subepithelial deposits are seen. Which of the following is a characteristic of this patient’s disease?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Antibodies to alveolar basement membrane
opb. Antibodies to phospholipase A2 receptor
opc. IgA immune complex deposition
opd. Loss of podocyte foot processes
ope. X-linked condition

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The patient's presentation with foamy urine, proteinuria, swelling in hands and feet, and findings of basement membrane thickening with subepithelial deposits on renal biopsy are indicative of membranous nephropathy. This condition is characterized by IgG immune complex deposition, specifically antibodies to phospholipase A2 receptor, not IgA immune complex deposition. Therefore, the characteristic of this patient's disease is antibodies to phospholipase A2 receptor (opb).
